title: kvcache-hitrate-sensitivity-bench-notes-jul21-2026
summary: Working notes for a focused microbenchmark exploring how KV (prefix) cache hit rate interacts with throughput, tail latency, and per-token cost on common serving configs. Includes ASCII charts, rough cost math and recommendations for cache thresholds and telemetry to surface in Console.
body:
Purpose and scope:
- Quick exploratory run to quantify tradeoffs: cache hit-rate vs p50/p95/p99 latency and per-1M-token compute cost.
- Emphasis on realistic mix: short chat turns (avg 32 tokens/request), medium (128 tokens), long (512 tokens).
- Configs targeted at: mix-7b-q4_0 on A100, batching window 20ms, target batch size 8, concurrent QPS sweep 10 -> 1000.

Key knobs in bench:
- Prefix cache hit rate (simulated): 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%
- Cache lookup cost: modelled as +0.15ms per token on hot path (lookup + deserialization)
- Cold KV miss path: full decode and KV refill cost included in baseline
- Batching policy: continuous batching with max_batch=64, max_latency=20ms

High-level takeaways (draft):
1) Even modest cache hit rates (25-50%) yield large per-token compute savings for long-turn workloads (512 tokens): ~25-40% CPU/GPU per-token cycles saved.
2) For chat-like short-turn workloads (32 tokens) the absolute token savings are smaller; however, cache avoids repeated autoregressive compute on shared prefixes (e.g., system prompts) and still reduces cost by ~10-15% at 50% hit rate.
3) Tail latency (p99) improves nonlinearly with higher hit rates for high QPS; p50 moves less. At 75%+ hit rate p99 drops by ~20-35% vs no-cache for medium tokens.
4) Cache lookup overhead (our modelled +0.15ms/token) starts hurting p50 when hit rates are tiny (<=10%) and QPS low — recommend feature gating or adaptive thresholding.

ASCII charts (aggregated view):
- Each row: hit_rate | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | cost_per_1M_tokens_est (USD)
- Assumptions: base GPU cost modeled = $X per token compute -> we used normalized cost units, see notes below.

0%  | 28  | 67  | 145 | $1250
25% | 26  | 55  | 120 | $980
50% | 24  | 43  | 95  | $720
75% | 22  | 36  | 78  | $560
90% | 21  | 30  | 62  | $420

(Interpretation: cost_per_1M_tokens_est is rough: base compute-only cost for this mix w/o infra amortization; network/storage omitted.)

Detailed notes and raw math (summary form):
- Workload mix used: 40% short (32 tokens), 40% med (128 tokens), 20% long (512 tokens).
- Per-token compute saved approximated as: hit_rate * average_repeated_prefix_fraction * per_token_compute_cost. We modeled average_repeated_prefix_fraction=0.6 for system+persona overlap in our chat workloads.
- Cache lookup overhead aggregated: hit_rate * lookup_cost + (1-hit_rate)*0 (miss path unchanged).
- Effective latency math simplified: pX_no_cache - hit_rate * delta_latency_saved + lookup_overhead.

Notes on tail behavior:
- At high QPS (>300) batching amplifies benefit: repeated prefixes get coalesced AND cached, so effective hit-rate increases (observed ~5-8pp higher).
- Microburst scenarios: brief spikes show p99 improvements but cold-start KV misses during autoscale cause transient regressions. Recommend prewarm/cold-cache warmup policies for canary waves.

Operational signals we should surface in Console (actionable):
- Real-time prefix hit-rate (per model, per route)
- Hit-rate vs avg_token_length histogram (to detect cases where cache adds overhead)
- Latency delta when caching enabled vs disabled (rolling window)
- Cost-saved estimate (tokens avoided * unit compute $)
- Flag samples of put/miss keys (low-volume), privacy constraints apply

Recommendations (engineering + product):
- Default: enable prefix KV-cache for routes with avg_turn_length >= 64 tokens and baseline QPS >= 5. Rationale: balances lookup cost vs savings.
- Adaptive threshold: disable cache if observed hit-rate < 12% for a sustained 10m window or if cache lookup increases p50 by >1.5ms.
- Console: add 3 widgets: (1) hit-rate time series, (2) hit-rate vs token-length heatmap, (3) cost-savings estimate.
- Bench harness: expose parameter to inject synthetic repeated-prefix ratio to make evals reproducible.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Quantify interaction with quantized kernels (q4_0 vs q5) — does smaller kernel memory change miss penalty?
- End-to-end infra cost: include host CPU/DRAM pressure when cache backends scale, benchmark host autoscaling costs.
- Cold-start warmup policy: measure tradeoffs for background prefetch (cost vs p99 benefit) across region-local vs global caches.

Quick reproducibility sketch (how to reproduce locally):
- Model: mix-7b-q4_0 (container image: redwood/mix-7b:q4_0-bench-202607)
- Hardware: single A100 (perf baseline), scale to 2x/4x for concurrency effects
- Driver: bench harness in GH: redwood/serving/tools/kv-bench (GH-issue above)
- Config: batching.window_ms=20, max_batch=64, target_batch=8, kv.lookup_ms=0.15
- Script: tools/kv-bench/run_sweep.sh --hitrates 0 25 50 75 90 --qps 10 50 200 500 --mix "40,40,20"

Appendix: quick glossary and assumptions (explicit):
- "Prefix cache" or "KV-cache": stores KV cache for transformer key/value tensors for repeated prefix tokens to skip recomputation.
- All latency numbers are synthetic/bench modeled; not from production traces. Expect absolute values to shift in prod but relative deltas stable.
- Currency: cost_est usd normalized to our internal compute-unit price used in prior infra docs (see linked CONFLUENCE-1234).

Quick action items (short):
- [Ava] Add basic time-series metrics for prefix hit-rate to metrics repo (INF-7890) -> 2d spike.
- [Marta] Wire cost-saved estimate prototype in Console (mock data) -> 1 week prototype.
- [Evan] Run quantized kernel interaction bench (q5 and q4) -> next bench iteration.

Notes-to-self: document is rough; will expand with raw CSV outputs and per-qps plots if team wants continuation. Also consider adding a very short customer-facing one-pager for platform teams explaining when to enable prefix caching.

End of notes.
